title: Exceptional composition and proper-square exchange under a cohomological comparison
statement:
Fix two correspondences $c,\bar c$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$, and a compactifiable cohomological pre-comparison $(f_Z,t_Z,\alpha_g,\beta_g,\iota)$ of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. Use its dualizing comparisons $\delta_Z$, ordinary mates $\alpha_{g,*}$ and exceptional mates $\beta_{g,!}$, with the constructible adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility]. The following identities hold on their finite-Tor constructible domains.

(a) Exceptional composition: $\beta_{\operatorname{id}}=\operatorname{id}$ and $\beta_{hg}=\bar g^!(\beta_h)\circ\beta_g(h^!(-))$, under the exceptional composition identifications.

(b) Dualizing composition: for every diagram arrow $g:U\to V$,
$$\delta_U=\bar g^!(\delta_V)\circ\beta_g(\omega_V)$$
under $g^!\omega_V=\omega_U$ and $\bar g^!\omega_{\bar V}=\omega_{\bar U}$ of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition].

(c) Let $h:U\to W$, $v:V\to W$, $U'=V\times_WU$, $h':U'\to V$, $v':U'\to U$ form a Cartesian square of arrows in the unbarred fixed diagram, and assume the corresponding barred square is Cartesian. Suppose $h,h',\bar h,\bar h'$ are proper. Let $E:Rh'_*v'^!\xrightarrow{\sim}v^!Rh_*$ and $\bar E:R\bar h'_*\bar v'^!\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar v^!R\bar h_*$ be the right-adjoint fixed-square exchange maps, normalized as mates of compact-support exchange. Then for every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$,
$$\bar v^!(\alpha_{h,*})\circ\beta_v(Rh_*M)\circ f_V(E_M)=\bar E_{f_UM}\circ R\bar h'_*(\beta_{v'}(M))\circ\alpha_{h',*}(v'^!M)$$
as maps $f_VRh'_*v'^!M\to\bar v^!R\bar h_*f_UM$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.1(a),(b),(c2), using proper direct-image identifications as in §4.4.6

proof.text:
Write $L_g=Rg_!$, $R_g=g^!$, $P_g=Rg_*$, and put $A_g=\alpha_{g,*}$ and $B_g=\beta_{g,!}$. Composition identifications will always be the adjunction-compatible ones. By [def-trf-admissibility] these adjunctions are on the specified finite-Tor constructible categories, and exceptional composition is conjugate to compact-support composition. Clause (3) of [prop-functor-package] supplies the identity and associative compact-support compositors and $L_g=P_g$ for proper $g$. The formula defining $B_g$ in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison] says equivalently
$$\bar\varepsilon_g\circ\bar L_g\beta_g=f_V(\varepsilon_g)\circ B_g(R_g(-)).\tag{1}$$
Indeed both sides are the transpose defining the mate, with the unit followed by a triangle identity, as in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. This identity does not require $g$ to be proper.

First work on compactifications supplied by axiom (VII) of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison], denoting the extended data by a superscript $*$. All its objects are proper over $k$. Indeed $X^*,C^*$ are proper by (VII); $X^*\times X^*$ is proper by base change and composition [lem-kun-proper-stability]. The diagonal is closed by separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The fixed scheme is its base change to $C^*$ [def-trf-fixed-scheme], so it too is proper by [lem-kun-proper-stability]. The same holds barred. Every arrow $g^*$ between these objects is therefore proper by [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target]. Axiom (III), followed by the mate-pasting law [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], gives
$$A^*_{hg}=(P_{\bar h^*}A^*_g)\circ(A^*_hP_{g^*}),\qquad A^*_{\mathrm{id}}=1.$$
Here the adjunctions being pasted are $g^{**}\dashv P_{g^*}$ and their barred versions; the ordinary mates are precisely the counit-defined maps of §4.1.1(c)(iv). Axiom (VI) identifies $B^*_g=(A^*_g)^{-1}$, and hence, by taking inverses of the displayed product,
$$B^*_{hg}=(B^*_hL_{g^*})\circ(\bar L_{h^*}B^*_g),\qquad B^*_{\mathrm{id}}=1.$$
Taking exceptional mates with [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clause (2), now proves $\beta^*_{hg}=\bar R_{g^*}(\beta^*_h)\circ\beta^*_g(R_{h^*}(-))$ and $\beta^*_{\mathrm{id}}=1$.

Here are the restriction identifications needed to descend that equality, without restricting an ordinary pushforward across an arbitrary open. For an open inclusion $j_T:T\hookrightarrow T^*$ write $J_T=j_{T!}$ and $Q_T=j_T^*$. The exact adjunction $J_T\dashv Q_T$ is [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]; it restricts to our categories by [lem-trf-open-ctf] and the pullback domains of [def-trf-admissibility]. The identity $Q_TJ_T=1$ is the degreewise identity $j^{-1}j_!=1$ in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. For $g^*j_U=j_Vg$, compact-support composition gives $L_{g^*}J_U=J_VL_g$. Taking the right-adjoint conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] gives the canonical identification
$$Q_UR_{g^*}=R_gQ_V.$$
The analogous identifications hold in the barred diagram. For composable arrows their two iterated identifications agree: they are the conjugates of the same associative compact-support composition, by [prop-functor-package], clause (3), and the composition rule in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate].

proof.text:
Let $N\in D^b_{ctf}(W,A)$ be an arbitrary input for $g:U\to V$, $h:V\to W$. Extend it to $J_WN$, which is in the compactified constructible domain by [lem-trf-open-ctf]. Restrict the equality of Step 2 on this input to $\bar U$. Axiom (VII)'s extension isomorphisms identify $\bar Q_Tf_T^*$ with $f_TQ_T$ and identify the restricted exceptional comparisons with $\beta_g,\beta_h,\beta_{hg}$ [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. The identifications of Step 3 identify all the exceptional composites and their inputs, and $Q_WJ_WN=N$. The restricted equality is therefore
$$\beta_{hg}(N)=\bar R_g(\beta_h(N))\circ\beta_g(R_hN).$$
For the identity arrow the same restriction gives $\beta_{\mathrm{id}}=1$. This proves (a) on every object, rather than only on objects already presented as restrictions. Taking its exceptional mates using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clause (2), also gives, now for all diagram arrows,
$$B_{hg}=(B_hL_g)\circ(\bar L_hB_g).\tag{2}$$

For (b), put $h=a_V$ in (a), so $a_U=a_Vg$. By [def-trf-cohomological-comparison], $\delta_U=\bar R_{a_U}(\iota)\circ\beta_{a_U}(A_s)$. Substitution of (a) and functoriality of $\bar R_g$ give
$$\delta_U=\bar R_g\bigl(\bar R_{a_V}(\iota)\circ\beta_{a_V}(A_s)\bigr)\circ\beta_g(R_{a_V}A_s)=\bar R_g(\delta_V)\circ\beta_g(\omega_V).$$
The identifications $R_g\omega_V=\omega_U$ and their barred counterparts are exactly [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]; thus this is the claimed equality with its specified dualizing identifications.

For (c), use the proper identifications $L_h=P_h$ and $L_{h'}=P_{h'}$, and likewise barred. Write
$$C:L_vL_{h'}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_hL_{v'},\qquad \bar C:\bar L_v\bar L_{h'}\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar L_h\bar L_{v'}$$
for the composition identifications from $vh'=hv'$, supplied by [prop-functor-package], clause (3). The last assertion of [lem-trf-trace-map-exchange] states precisely the normalization of the right-adjoint exchange used here: the $L_v\dashv R_v$ transpose of $E_M$ is
$$L_vL_{h'}R_{v'}M\xrightarrow{C}L_hL_{v'}R_{v'}M\xrightarrow{L_h\varepsilon_{v'}}L_hM.\tag{3}$$
It applies since our square is Cartesian, $h$ is proper and all its arrows have the constructible adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility]. Applying that assertion to the barred Cartesian square gives the identical formula for $\bar E$. Thus no claim that a general square mate preserves isomorphisms is being used.

Apply (2) to the two factorizations $vh'=hv'$. Associative composition identifies their common map $B_{vh'}=B_{hv'}$, and gives
$$f_W(C)\circ B_v(L_{h'}(-))\circ\bar L_vB_{h'}
=B_h(L_{v'}(-))\circ\bar L_hB_{v'}\circ\bar C.\tag{4}$$
Axiom (VI) of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison] gives $B_h=A_h^{-1}$ and $B_{h'}=A_{h'}^{-1}$. Precompose (4) with $\bar L_vA_{h'}$ and postcompose with $A_h(L_{v'}(-))$. The two inverse pairs cancel, yielding
$$A_h(L_{v'}(-))\circ f_W(C)\circ B_v(L_{h'}(-))
=\bar L_hB_{v'}\circ\bar C\circ\bar L_vA_{h'}.\tag{5}$$
All components in (4) and (5) are evaluated on a variable object of $D^b_{ctf}(U',A)$; we will use that object $R_{v'}M$. This is cancellation of the two proper comparison isomorphisms, with no inversion of $B_v$ or $B_{v'}$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.1(c2), composition and adjointness; §4.4.6 use of axiom (VI)

proof.text:
Transpose the left side of the equality in (c) under $\bar L_v\dashv\bar R_v$. By naturality of its counit, equation (1) for $v$, naturality of $B_v$ with respect to $E_M$, and (3), the result is
$$T_L=A_h(M)\circ f_W(L_h\varepsilon_{v',M})\circ f_W(C_{R_{v'}M})\circ B_v(L_{h'}R_{v'}M).\tag{6}$$
Explicitly, (1) replaces $\bar\varepsilon_v\circ\bar L_v\beta_v$ by $f_W(\varepsilon_v)\circ B_vR_v$; naturality moves $\bar L_vf_V(E_M)$ across $B_v$, leaving $f_W(\varepsilon_v\circ L_vE_M)$, which is (3). The same transpose of the right side, using the barred formula (3), naturality of $\bar C$ and equation (1) for $v'$, is
$$T_R=\bar L_h(f_U\varepsilon_{v',M})\circ\bar L_h(B_{v'}(R_{v'}M))\circ\bar C_{f_{U'}R_{v'}M}\circ\bar L_v(A_{h'}(R_{v'}M)).\tag{7}$$
These computations use only the mate definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] and the normalized exchange assertion [lem-trf-trace-map-exchange], with the adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility].

Naturality of $A_h$ at $\varepsilon_{v',M}:L_{v'}R_{v'}M\to M$ gives
$$A_h(M)\circ f_W(L_h\varepsilon_{v',M})=\bar L_h(f_U\varepsilon_{v',M})\circ A_h(L_{v'}R_{v'}M).$$
Insert this in (6), then substitute (5) evaluated at $R_{v'}M$. The resulting composite is exactly (7), so $T_L=T_R$. The Hom bijection for $\bar L_v\dashv\bar R_v$ in [def-trf-admissibility] is injective, hence the original two maps agree. Replacing the four proper $L$'s by their specified $P$'s proves exactly the displayed equation (c), with source $f_VRh'_*v'^!M$ and target $\bar v^!R\bar h_*f_UM$.

split_report.summary: Expanded the proper-compactification, restriction, and mate arguments of Varshavsky Lemma 4.2.1 into nine steps. Reused the existing mate-pasting Mathlib leaf, open extension facts, and the exact proper-square transpose normalization already stated by lem-trf-trace-map-exchange. Statement unchanged; no new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Nearest blueprint ancestor lem-trf-local-term-locality, proof of contracting local terms by normal-cone specialization (unit sk-i-curve-zero step 2): realizes the exceptional composition, dualizing and proper fixed-square comparison input used in lem-trf-trace-specialization, via the trace-specialization intermediate.

tool_uses.why: The generic proper-source/separated-target criterion verifies properness of arrows in the compactified fixed diagrams.
Open extension preserves the finite-Tor constructible domain, allowing arbitrary inputs to be extended before restricting the compactified identity.
The exact open-extension adjunction supplies the right-adjoint restriction calculation without an ambient exceptional adjoint.
Uses only the open localization identity j inverse-image j shriek = identity to recover arbitrary inputs from their extensions.
Uses only the existing compact-support composition, associativity, and proper-coincidence clause (3), as a geometric operation tool.
Uses solely its independent final assertion computing the exceptional transpose of normalized right-adjoint exchange for an arbitrary Cartesian square with proper horizontal map.
Generic properness stability shows the compactified product and fixed scheme are proper, before applying axiom (VI).
The compactified diagonal is proper because it is a closed immersion; this verifies the compactification reduction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NW-4e1a8cf2e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery, and the mathematics holds up; no fixes needed. The item statement is unchanged from the base (compared against the side DAG), and it matches Varshavsky Lemma 4.2.1(a), 4.2.1(b) and (c2)+axiom (VI) as used in §4.4.6 (printed pp. 26-30 and 38), clause by clause. The mate types match §4.1.1(c)(iv),(v). E is the conjugate-of-Ex_! exchange of def-trf-admissibility on D^b_ctf(-,A). I checked every calculation by hand: equation (1) by triangle identity; Step 2 properness of the compactified objects and arrows (product, closed diagonal, Fix as base change, then nagata-proper-to-separated-target), then (III)->(VI)->mates via mate-pasting; Step 3 Q_U R_{g*}=R_g Q_V as the conjugate of L_{g*}J_U=J_V L_g, with no Cartesian square needed; Step 4 descent through J_W, with F=F*∩C; Step 5 (b) by substitution; Steps 7-9 type-checked, with only A_h and A_{h'} cancelled; transposes (6) and (7) recomputed and they agree. Each cited statement says what its step takes from it, and no SGA source is used. There is no cycle; the only citer is lem-trf-trace-specialization, which uses (c) with h=Δ, v=c, h'=i_F, v'=d, in the right orientation. There are no new nodes and no duplicates; lem-trf-cohomological-evaluation-calculus is different and is not used. On the unit route (sk-i-curve-zero), only lem-trf-open-ctf and the generic final clause of lem-trf-trace-map-exchange are off-route. Both are declared, generic, and not supplied by any node on the route, so I accept both tool uses. Minor point, not a fault: the hypotheses h', h̄' proper are redundant because they follow by base change.
